  echo "committed?=$( [ -n \"$(git log --oneline -1 -- $P)\" ] && echo YES || echo NO )"

reports **YES for the UNCOMMITTED file** and **NO for a committed control**. Reproduced side by side in one call. With no commits the test degrades to `[ -n ]`, and a one-argument `[` tests whether the string `-n` is non-empty — which it is — so it is TRUE. With a real commit line it becomes `[ -n a1b2c3d some subject ]` -> `[: too many arguments` -> NO.   OUT=$(git log --oneline -1 -- <path>); echo "len=${#OUT}"    # assign first, then test
